sections.title: Getting started
sections.summary: Create a Figure or Presentation, add artwork, and keep an editable copy.
body: Choose Figure for manuscript panels, graphical abstracts, diagrams, and illustrations. Choose Presentation for a slide deck with layouts, themes, notes, and playback. Use the Figure / Presentation buttons to switch between them.

Use File > New to choose a document type and size. Library contains Assets, Scenes, and Templates. The canvas is where you draw and arrange artwork; Style or Inspector shows controls for the current selection. Simple keeps common controls close at hand; Advanced exposes detailed vector and text controls.

Use Document setup to change page dimensions, units, grids, and snapping without clearing your selection. Fit brings the artboard back into view. Changing canvas zoom does not change the size of exported artwork.

In the web app, use Appearance · Light / Dark in the header. In Superbench, use App Settings. This changes the interface without recoloring artwork. Browser files contains Saved work, Open file, Download file, and About. Browser saves stay on this device; download an editable file for backup or use on another computer.
Start with the topics on selecting artwork, Lines and arrows, and saving work. Help provides reference instructions and short visual demonstrations for the current tools.

sections.title: Switching between Figure and Presentation
sections.summary: Switch workspaces while keeping documents in both open.
body: Use Figure or Presentation in the header. Figure provides an illustration canvas; Presentation adds a slide navigator, slide layouts, notes, and Present controls.
Each workspace has its own document tabs. Switching workspaces returns to the last active tab without closing the other documents.

New and Open activate the workspace appropriate to the document. Save and Export apply to the active document. Save Project preserves all open Figure and Presentation tabs together in an .fsproject file.
Present starts playback of a Presentation; it does not change the document type or save the deck.

sections.title: Working with document tabs
sections.summary: Keep several documents open and switch between them above the canvas.
body: Use File > New or Open to add a document. The + button beside the tab strip opens New. Use Figure / Presentation to reach tabs in the other workspace.
Each open tab keeps its artwork, selection, view, and Undo / Redo history separately. A marker beside its name indicates changes that have not been saved to its document file.
Use the close button on a tab to close that document. If it has unsaved changes, cancel the confirmation to keep it open and save first. Closing a clean tab does not close other tabs.

Open Project replaces the complete open workspace. Save Project first if you want to keep its collection of documents. Portable files preserve artwork and document settings, but not transient selection or Undo history.
Browser autosave preserves the open workspace separately from downloaded files. Closing a document changes that workspace; use Download file or Download project to keep a deliberate copy.

sections.title: Creating a Figure
sections.summary: Start with a blank artboard, layout, or editable scientific scene.
body: Choose File > New, select Figure, and choose a preset or custom dimensions. The white artboard defines the exported page.
Open Library > Templates for a clean canvas, graphical abstract, or multi-panel Figure. A template creates a new document; earlier Figures remain open in their tabs.

Add individual symbols from Assets, or use a complete diagram from Scenes. Add labels with Text and relationships with Lines. Frames and panel labels are editable artwork rather than fixed image placeholders.

Document setup controls units, artboard dimensions, grids, guides, and multi-panel layout. Review the Figure at its intended final size, then save an .fsfigure copy and use Export for a delivery file.

sections.title: Sizing artboards and arranging panels
sections.summary: Set the exported page size and arrange editable panel frames.
body: Open Document setup for Units, Artboard presets, Width, and Height. Changing the page dimensions does not automatically rescale existing artwork.

Use the multi-panel Rows and Columns controls and Create layout to add panel frames and labels. Add title + legend inserts editable text placeholders. Replace their text and adjust frames to suit the results.
Use Align and Distribute for consistent edges and gaps. Guides help position artwork; snapping can be enabled separately for grids, guides, and objects.
Fit artboard restores an overview. Pan and zoom to inspect details. Drawing and selecting preserve the current view; use Fit explicitly when you want the artboard fitted again.
Normal export clips to the chosen artboard. Artwork outside it remains editable; move important content inside the page before exporting.

sections.title: Creating a Presentation
sections.summary: Build a slide deck with consistent dimensions, themes, and notes.
body: Choose File > New, select Presentation, and choose Widescreen, Standard, or custom dimensions. All slides use the deck dimensions.
Use New slide and the Slides navigator to build the deck. Layout & theme provides starting arrangements and coordinated type and color choices; the artwork remains editable.
Draw, import, add scientific assets, and arrange objects with the same authoring tools used for Figures. Notes stores speaker notes for the selected slide.

Save an .fsdeck copy to retain the editable deck. Use PDF for visual sharing or PPTX for supported editable slide content. Review exported files before presenting; complex artwork may be flattened or omitted in PPTX with warnings.

sections.title: Managing slides, layouts, themes, and notes
sections.summary: Add and arrange slides, then keep their text and appearance consistent.
body: Use New slide to add a slide. Select a thumbnail in Slides to edit it; use slide actions to duplicate, move, or delete it. Reordering keeps its artwork and notes together.
Open Layout & theme to apply a layout or theme. Layout objects remain editable. Check text wrapping and deliberate custom colors after changes.
Open Notes for the selected slide and enter speaker notes. Notes are saved in .fsdeck and supported PPTX output; they are not included as visible artwork in normal slide images or PDFs.
Use Present to review the complete deck. Keep panel labels, type sizes, and scientific symbols readable at the projected size.

sections.title: Presenting a slide deck
sections.summary: Play the active Presentation and return to editing afterward.
body: Present from beginning starts at slide 1. Present from current slide starts at the selected slide. Both use the active Presentation tab.
Playback fits the complete slide to the available window. Use the visible navigation controls or keyboard navigation to move between slides. Open Notes to view the current slide’s speaker notes.
Exit or Escape returns to editing. Playback does not change slide geometry, save the document, or export a file.
Review small type, cropped content, image legibility, and the order of your scientific argument before presenting to an audience.

sections.title: Opening and importing artwork
sections.summary: Open SVG or PDF as a Figure, or insert artwork into an existing document.
body: Choose File > New, then Open PDF or SVG to start a Figure from artwork. File > Open PDF also opens a PDF directly. Use File > Import SVG/Image/PDF when artwork should be inserted into the current Figure or slide. Review its placement and dimensions before continuing.

For PDF, choose Editable reconstruction to create supported canvas text and vectors, or Source-backed placement to keep the page together with its original PDF. Select the first page, all pages, or a page range where offered. The import summary tells you what was actually reconstructed and what remains a placed preview.

PDF text may be reconstructed as editable text or kept as outlines depending on the source and supported import path. Font replacement can alter labels or spacing. Compare the result with the original PDF; unsupported or dense pages may fall back to a placed page.

Press A for Direct Selection to reach editable children in a supported imported group. A placed image or protected page does not expose individual vector anchors. Source details identify the retained original, page, and import limitations.
The web app supports PDF placement and supported reconstruction in the browser. Advanced changes to the original PDF require the desktop PDF service and are unavailable on a static website.
Raster images retain their source pixels. Vectorization can turn visible pixel regions into editable shapes; it does not recover the original plot data, labels, or biological meaning.

sections.title: Working with PowerPoint files
sections.summary: Exchange common editable slide content and review warnings for unsupported objects.
body: PPTX import and export support slide order, one uniform slide size, ordinary text boxes, basic shapes, straight lines and connectors, embedded PNG/JPEG/SVG images, basic solid fills and strokes, arrowheads, and plain speaker notes.

Basic font, size, bold, italic, alignment, and text color are retained where supported. Mixed character formatting, including superscript, subscript, and baseline shift, may be reduced to the text object’s base style with a warning. Check scientific notation after interchange.

Artwork that cannot be represented as an editable PowerPoint object may be embedded as SVG, or omitted if it cannot be safely represented. Read import and export warnings; a visible SVG image is not the same as independently editable shapes.

SmartArt, charts, tables, media, animations, transitions, macros, OLE objects, arbitrary freeform paths, and complex theme or master content are not fully supported. Objects inherited from masters or layouts are not reconstructed as ordinary slide artwork.

Google Slides use is file-based through PPTX or visual exports. There is no direct Google Drive or Google Slides connection. Keep the original file and inspect the exported deck in the application where it will be used.

sections.title: Selecting and arranging artwork
sections.summary: Select artwork on the canvas or in Layers, then move, group, hide, or lock it.
body: Use Select or press V to select whole objects. Click an object, Shift-click to extend the selection, or drag across empty canvas to select several. Use the selection handles to resize or rotate; drag the selected artwork to move it.
Right-click selected artwork for duplicate, delete, group, ungroup, arrange, hide, lock, and property commands. Only applicable actions are available for protected or locked artwork.

Open Inspector > Layers to select and rename objects, expand groups, and change visibility or locks. Reveal in Layers finds selected canvas artwork; Select on canvas selects an object from its row. Fit selection brings it into view.

New artwork goes into the current named layer. Use Move here or the layer context menu to move a selection. Drag eligible object rows before, inside, or after a compatible destination; the destination highlight shows the intended change.

Double-click a group to edit its children in Isolation Mode. Back or Escape returns to the containing artwork. Group and layer edits preserve placement and can be undone; protected imported groups may offer fewer actions.

sections.title: Positioning, aligning, and distributing artwork
sections.summary: Use whole-object selection for arrangement and Direct Selection for individual points.
body: Select or V moves, resizes, and rotates whole objects. Direct Selection or A edits supported path anchors, line endpoints, and connector bends. Drag a Direct Selection box from empty canvas to discover editable anchors, including those on unselected artwork. Shift extends the point selection.

Style or Inspector provides numeric position and size controls. Advanced exposes rotation, shear, exact gaps, and additional transforms where applicable. Line geometry includes start/end coordinates, length, and angle; selecting one endpoint keeps the opposite endpoint fixed during length or angle changes.

Align and Distribute can use the selected artwork, artboard, or a chosen key object. A key object remains fixed while the other objects move. Use exact gaps when panel spacing needs a specific measurement.

View contains separate Snap to Grid, Snap to Guides, and Snap to Objects choices. Smart Guides controls the temporary alignment cues. Hold Ctrl (Command on macOS) while moving, scaling, or drawing to bypass snapping for that gesture.

In Figure mode, Duplicate and Repeat and Transform Again can reuse a supported previous transform. They are unavailable for artwork where repeating could break a source relationship or connector. Undo returns the artwork to its previous placement.

sections.title: Editing shapes, paths, and anchors
sections.summary: Draw editable geometry and select individual points without first selecting the object.
body: Choose Shapes for basic geometric objects, or Pen for a custom path. With Pen, click to add straight anchors and drag to create curved handles. Return to the first anchor to close a path, or press Enter to finish an open path.

Press A for Direct Selection. Click a path or drag a selection box across its anchors; a box can find editable anchors even when the object was not previously selected. Shift adds points to the selection. Drag selected points to change the shape, then use Undo if needed.

Press Delete to remove selected anchors. If enough points remain, the path reconnects. If fewer than two points remain in an open path or three in a closed path, the affected path or subpath is removed. Other parts of an isolated asset remain in place. Deleting an endpoint of an ordinary line removes that line. Undo restores the artwork and point selection.

Curve direction handles become available when their path or anchor is selected. Direct Selection also edits line endpoints and connector bends. It does not turn an image, locked object, or protected source page into freely editable geometry.

Double-click an editable group to enter Isolation Mode, then select its child artwork. Back or Escape returns to the containing group. Imported SVG and PDF editing depends on what the importer could represent; keep the source and compare important details visually.

Use point controls to change supported anchor types, add or remove nodes, or refine a segment. Shape Builder combines regions of eligible closed shapes; Alt removes a region. Compound paths preserve multiple subpaths in one editable object.

sections.title: Drawing lines and arrows
sections.summary: Choose a graphical preset, then draw it or apply it to a selected line.
body: Open Lines to see previews for plain lines, arrows, inhibition bars, dots, curved or circular routes, brackets, and custom drawing. Scroll the menu for the remaining groups.

Choose Draw new, select a preset, and drag on the canvas. Straight and curved presets use their own drawing tools. Smart connectors attach to object ports; comparison brackets require the appropriate selected objects.

To restyle an existing eligible line, select it, open Lines, choose Apply to selected, and click a preset. Presets for unavailable conversions are disabled; protected imported artwork must first become editable.

Style or the Advanced stroke controls provide color, width, dash, and start/end markers. Press A to adjust endpoints or supported bends. Geometry measurements appear while you draw or edit; numeric controls remain available in Inspector.

Use arrow and inhibition styles consistently in a scientific diagram. A symbol does not establish a biological interaction by itself; label an ambiguous relationship and distinguish proposed relationships from measured results.

sections.title: Connecting diagram objects
sections.summary: Attach lines to objects so relationships follow their movement.
body: Open Lines and choose a smart connector, then choose its start and end object ports. Eligible objects expose ports along their edges. Straight, elbow, and curved routes have editable stroke, dash, marker, and label settings.

Use Select to select the connector as one object. Press A for Direct Selection to edit an endpoint or elbow bend. Drag an endpoint onto a port to attach it; drag it into empty canvas to detach that endpoint.

Shift constrains endpoint or bend movement to one axis. Alt, Ctrl, or Command bypasses ports and snapping for free movement. Arrow keys nudge a selected handle; Shift makes a larger step. Reverse exchanges the relationship direction.

Editing an elbow bend creates a manual route. Auto returns to automatic routing; Orthogonal keeps manual legs axis-aligned. Automatic routing avoids supported obstacles but cannot resolve every crossing in a crowded diagram.

Connector labels are editable text. Move a label to offset it from the route, or use Label home to restore automatic placement. Moving connected nodes updates the line. Save and reopen retain endpoint connections, bends, labels, and offsets.

sections.title: Formatting text and scientific symbols
sections.summary: Keep labels editable and check their readability at the final figure size.
body: Use Text or T to add a label; drag with Text to create a fixed text frame. Character and Paragraph controls provide font, size, spacing, weight, alignment, and text direction. Advanced exposes additional type controls.

While editing text, select characters for Superscript, Subscript, or Baseline shift. With a caret, the choice applies to newly typed characters. Symbols lets you search Greek letters, mathematical notation, arrows, and units and insert them at the caret.

A fixed text frame reflows when its width changes. A plus badge or overset status means some text does not fit. Fit frame to content increases its height; review wrapping and the final exported result.
For text on a path, select an ordinary editable text object and path, then choose Type > Type on a Path. Use path offset/alignment controls to position it; Detach from Path returns separate objects.

Create Outlines converts supported live text to vector glyphs. Restore Editable Text can return retained source text. Complex scripts and advanced font shaping are not fully supported, so check outlined text carefully.

Type > Publication typography coordinates panel labels, titles, annotations, and legend text. Review its proposed size and style changes before Apply. It does not certify a journal’s requirements or the readability of every imported label.

PDF imports can use editable text, font replacement, or outlines depending on the source. The document retains supported character styles, while PPTX may reduce mixed formatting. Review scientific notation and fonts in the final destination.

sections.title: Layering fills, strokes, and effects
sections.summary: Apply several paints to one editable vector object.
body: Select an ordinary editable shape or path and open Appearance in Inspector, or use Object appearance commands in Advanced. The top appearance row is painted in front of lower rows.

Add fills or strokes using solid colors, gradients, or supported patterns. Each row has its own visibility, opacity, and blend mode; stroke rows also have a width. Offset Copy and Soft Shadow add supported effects.
Press G or choose Edit on canvas to edit a gradient. Drag its endpoints or center/radius and color stops. Double-click its axis to add a stop; select an interior stop and press Delete to remove it.

Expand Appearance turns eligible paint stacks into ordinary grouped artwork. Patterns or shadows can prevent expansion. Reduce to Base Appearance removes additional paints. Both operations should be reviewed visually.

Up to eight appearance items and eight authored gradient stops are supported. Text, groups, lines, protected imports, and native PDF objects use their own controls. Save and reopen retain supported appearance settings; export may differ for unsupported effects.

sections.title: Reusing Graphic Styles
sections.summary: Save an object’s appearance and apply it to other editable vectors.
body: Select an ordinary editable shape or path. Open Object > Graphic Styles or My Assets, enter a style name, and choose Save selection. Appearance also offers Save style for an eligible selected vector.

Choose a style thumbnail to replace the appearance of eligible selected vectors. Merge or the plus control adds its paints in front of existing paints. At most eight appearance items are retained; omitted items are reported.
Rename or delete custom styles in My Assets. Built-in styles remain available. Saved document files retain custom styles, and style changes can be undone.

Locked objects, text, lines, groups, and protected imports are not eligible for these vector styles. Use their dedicated text, line, or asset controls instead. Applying a style does not rewrite the original PDF.

sections.title: Saving colors and recoloring artwork
sections.summary: Reuse document colors and preview coordinated changes.
body: Open Inspector > Saved colors, or Object > Saved colors in Advanced. Add a named color, then apply it to eligible fills, strokes, text, markers, or a selected gradient stop.
A Global color keeps a link to the artwork that uses it: editing the color updates its linked uses. A Process color applies its current value without that continuing link.
Select > Same Fill Color, Same Stroke Color, and Same Global Swatch find related artwork. Collect adds colors from an eligible selected group to the document color library.
Choose Recolor Selection to map existing colors to new values or saved colors. Review the live preview, then Apply colors; Cancel restores the starting appearance.

Colors are saved in .fsfigure and .fsdeck files. Protected PDF artwork is not recolored by ordinary swatch controls. Add labels, patterns, or line styles when color alone would make a scientific comparison unclear.

sections.title: Creating vector patterns
sections.summary: Create a repeating tile from editable artwork and use it as a fill.
body: Select one to eight ordinary editable shapes or paths. Open Saved colors and choose Create in Patterns, or Object > Make Pattern from Selection in Advanced. The original artwork stays on the canvas.

Choose the pattern thumbnail for an eligible target. Named patterns can be reused in Appearance and Graphic Styles. Rename or delete them in Saved colors; deleting a library entry leaves current artwork with its existing unlinked tile.
Use Object > Edit Pattern Tile or Edit beside the pattern in Appearance. Adjust its origin, bounds, and spacing. Commit or Enter keeps the changes; Cancel or Escape restores the starting tile.

Document files retain the editable pattern library. SVG and PDF export supported vector appearance, but opening an exported file does not recreate the named library. Protected PDF patterns and gradient meshes are not freely rewritten by this tool.

sections.title: Using brushes and variable-width strokes
sections.summary: Apply width profiles, calligraphic strokes, or repeated vector artwork to a path.
body: Select an ordinary editable single-subpath path, line, or arrow. In Advanced, use Appearance or Object > Brush Options to choose a width profile, calligraphic brush, art brush, or scientific motif. Review the live preview before Apply.

Use Width Tool or Shift+W to adjust a stroke at individual points. Link sides keeps symmetric width; turn it off to adjust each side separately. Click to add a width point, nudge with arrow keys, or Delete an eligible interior point. Enter commits and Escape cancels the edit.

New Art Brush from Selection captures eligible vector artwork without removing it from the canvas. Options control direction, mirroring, stretch, and coloring. Text, raster images, protected PDF objects, and unsupported effects need a different approach or explicit conversion first.

Scientific motifs include schematic membranes, nucleic acids, vessels, actin, and microtubules. Adjust spacing, scale, direction, side, and colors. These drawings communicate a schematic idea; they do not establish molecular scale, composition, or interaction evidence.

Expand Art Brush to Paths replaces a live brush with grouped editable vector pieces. Ungroup or enter Isolation Mode to edit individual points. The expanded artwork no longer follows the live brush definition.

Dense motifs and self-intersecting curves can affect responsiveness or appearance. The editor reports count limits; increase spacing or shorten the path. Save retains supported brush settings, while SVG and PDF use the visible vector geometry. Pressure-sensitive, scatter, and bristle brushes are not provided.

sections.title: Clipping artwork and making compound paths
sections.summary: Keep artwork inside an editable clipping boundary or combine path subparts.
body: Place an ordinary editable clipping path above the content and select them together. Choose Object > Make Clipping Mask or Ctrl+7. Layers shows the clipping path and clipped contents separately.
Use Edit Clipping Path for its anchors, Edit Clipped Contents to enter the contents, or Release Clipping Mask to return the items to the canvas.

Select eligible paths and choose Object > Make Compound Path or Ctrl+8. Its subpaths share one object and an even-odd fill; Direct Selection can edit their anchors. Release Compound Path separates them.

Imported clips and masks are editable only when they can be represented safely. Unsupported source appearance stays protected. These controls do not provide unrestricted editing of every PDF mask or compositing effect.

sections.title: Using assets, scenes, and templates
sections.summary: Find scientific symbols or insert an editable diagram.
body: Open Library and choose Assets, Scenes, or Templates. Search and filters apply to the selected view. Assets contains individual symbols; Scenes contains editable diagrams; Templates provides new Figure layouts.

Use Favorites and Recent to find frequently used drawings. Related searches offers names from the matching catalog and keeps your current filters. Clear search removes only the query, keeping those filters.

Choose Preview on a drawing to inspect a larger image, alternate forms or views, scientific limitations, and editable parts. Close or Escape returns to the Library without inserting or changing artwork.
Style and Palette choices in the Library affect the next insertion. The preview states those choices; it does not recolor artwork already on the canvas. Library cards always insert a new drawing.

Select one inserted Library drawing and choose Change drawing in Style or the detailed Inspector; in Presentation, use Format. The chooser changes only the selected drawing by default. A counted checkbox can include other unlocked, unmodified copies on this figure or slide. If you edited the selected drawing, review and acknowledge that changing it discards those edits. Custom drawings remain editable with the canvas tools. Changing a drawing keeps its size, position and stacking order; one Undo restores its previous artwork. Closing the chooser leaves the canvas unchanged.

Part colors names the biological regions available in the selected drawing. Change a region color or reset it without changing the other parts. These controls affect the selected drawing; the Library Palette affects the next insertion.

For a scene, Use as new figure creates a new document. Insert in this figure or Insert on this slide adds it to the current canvas. Its labels, symbols, and relationships remain separately editable on named layers.

Edit placeholder labels to match your experiment or biological system. Check each arrow’s meaning and remove irrelevant branches. A reusable diagram is a starting point, not evidence for a particular biological claim.

Release editable paths only when you need detailed geometry changes; released paths stop behaving as one library asset. Original bundled artwork is offered for unrestricted reuse under CC0; imported third-party artwork retains its own permissions. Document setup > Sources & reuse records available source and rights information.

sections.title: Placing result panels, images, and tables
sections.summary: Arrange imported results while keeping their underlying image or artwork available.
body: Import a result SVG, image, or PDF into the current Figure or slide. Source & notes records available source information. In Advanced, Object > Link Selected Panel marks eligible imported artwork for explicit refresh. It does not watch your local file or analysis for automatic changes; a Superbench-hosted result can have additional source information.

Select an eligible image to use Image Frame controls. Fit shows the whole image, Fill crops within the frame, the focal control changes its position, and Reset removes frame adjustments. The source pixels remain available in the document.
Locked or protected artwork must become eligible before it can be reframed. Resizing an image does not increase its underlying resolution; inspect it at the final output size.
File > Import CSV/TSV Table creates a small publication table from a local file. It is intended for concise values and labels; it is not a spreadsheet calculator or bulk data editor.

sections.title: Reusing a group of artwork
sections.summary: Save an authored group and reuse linked copies of it.
body: Group ordinary authored artwork, open My Assets, enter a name under Scientific components, and choose Save group. Insert places another linked copy on the canvas.

Select an instance and open Instance overrides to change supported named-part text, colors, visibility, or opacity. Update master sends geometry changes to linked instances while keeping supported local overrides.

Reset removes a part’s override or all instance overrides. Detach makes an independent local copy. Rename or delete masters in My Assets; deleting a master detaches its existing instances rather than deleting their artwork.

Linked analysis panels, protected imports, native PDF content, locked descendants, and nested components cannot become masters. Use an ordinary editable group. Save and reopen retain supported component links and overrides.

sections.title: Saving and downloading an editable file
sections.summary: Keep one document as .fsfigure or .fsdeck, or all open documents as .fsproject.
body: Save and Save As apply to the active document. A Figure uses .fsfigure and a Presentation uses .fsdeck. Save Project preserves all open Figure and Presentation tabs together in an .fsproject file.

In the web app, Browser files > Download file downloads the active document. File > Save and Save As also download an editable file; the browser chooses its destination. This is separate from automatic browser storage.
Browser files > Saved work lists locally stored workspaces. Download project on a list entry preserves its open documents as .fsproject. Use Open file to reopen a downloaded document or project.

In the desktop app, Save on an untitled document opens a Windows save dialog. Later Save writes to its chosen path; Save As chooses a new name or location. A failed write does not clear the unsaved-change marker.

Legacy .figurestudio and .figure-studio.json files are accepted for import. Save them in a current format after reviewing their content. Export creates delivery files such as PNG, SVG, PDF, or PPTX; it does not replace your editable document.

In the desktop app, Save on an untitled document opens a Windows save dialog. Later Save writes to its chosen path; Save As chooses a new name or location. A failed write does not clear the unsaved-change marker.

Legacy .figurestudio and .figure-studio.json files are accepted for import. Save them in a current format after reviewing their content. Export creates delivery files such as PNG, SVG, PDF, or PPTX; it does not replace your editable document.

sections.title: Browser saves, reopening, and recovery
sections.summary: Use local autosave and downloaded backups for different purposes.
body: The web app automatically saves edits in this browser when storage is available. Browser files shows save status. Saved work lists locally stored workspaces with Resume, Rename, Download project, and Remove.

Earlier saves retains two previous snapshots. Recovering one opens a separate copy rather than overwriting the current saved work. If a save fails, keep the editor open, download a file, and use Retry. For competing-tab conflicts, save a separate copy or review which version you want to keep.

Browser copies stay on this device and browser profile. They do not sync to another computer or cloud account. Clearing site data removes them, and private browsing is not lasting storage. Download backups of important work.

Use Open file for .fsfigure, .fsdeck, or .fsproject. Individual files open as document tabs; a project restores its open workspace. Opening a project can replace current tabs, so preserve current work first.

Embedded images and bundled assets reopen without their original local folder. Missing linked artwork needs an available source or replacement; check Source & notes before changing it. Portable files retain artwork and settings, but not live Undo history.
On desktop, save to deliberate document files and keep ordinary backups. If a recovery copy is offered after an interruption, review it and use Save As. Recovery cannot guarantee every unsaved edit.

sections.title: Exporting a Figure
sections.summary: Choose a delivery format, final dimensions, and background.
body: Activate the intended Figure tab and choose Export. The dialog names the document and shows a preview. Select the required artboard scope where more than one is available.

SVG and PDF preserve supported vector artwork and do not use DPI settings. Imported image content remains raster. PDF is useful for a publication page; SVG is useful when another application can edit the supported vectors.
PNG, JPEG, and TIFF create raster output. Choose a DPI preset, scale, or explicit pixel dimensions. Output size depends on these settings and page dimensions, not the canvas zoom.
Choose a transparent or solid background where supported. JPEG is always opaque. Check image edges and antialiasing against the intended final background.

Export warnings identifies supported problems such as small or overset text, low-resolution images, missing artwork, or content outside the page. Click an artwork warning to locate it. Optional export check provides additional information; it does not replace visual review or assess scientific conclusions.
Open the exported file and inspect it at its intended final size. Keep the .fsfigure source. Browser exports download files; desktop exports use the destination offered by the installed app.

sections.title: Exporting a Presentation
sections.summary: Create a PDF, PowerPoint file, or images of selected slides.
body: Activate the intended Presentation and choose Export. The dialog names that deck. Use Current slide or All slides where the selected format provides that choice.

PDF creates pages in slide order. Check every page for missing content, font changes, and cropping. PPTX retains common editable objects but can flatten or skip complex artwork with warnings; read the PowerPoint compatibility topic.
PNG, JPEG, and TIFF provide resolution or pixel-dimension controls. Current slide produces one image; All slides produces consistently numbered outputs using the available folder or package option.
Background choices depend on the format. JPEG is opaque. Notes are saved in .fsdeck and supported PPTX notes, rather than painted into ordinary slide images or PDF pages.
Review warnings and open the final output in its intended viewer. Keep the editable .fsdeck source. A browser reports downloaded filenames but cannot know their final folder.

sections.title: Choosing a save or export format
sections.summary: Keep editable sources and select a separate output for sharing.
body: Use .fsfigure for one editable Figure, .fsdeck for one editable Presentation, and .fsproject for an open collection of both. Save these files even when another format is the deliverable.
SVG and PDF retain supported vector appearance. PNG, JPEG, and TIFF render pixels at your chosen dimensions. Neither a vector file extension nor high DPI restores detail missing from a source image.
PPTX is for supported editable slide content. Complex artwork may be embedded as an image or omitted with a warning. Review the result in PowerPoint or another receiving application.

Export previews and warnings help find output issues. Optional export check gives more detail when needed; it does not certify a figure or replace final-size visual review. Sources & reuse in Document setup helps inspect recorded artwork and permissions.

sections.title: Finding Help
sections.summary: Search task instructions and follow related topics without changing the document.
body: Open Help > Search Help. Search names such as lines, direct selection, browser saves, or PowerPoint. Browse the topic list when you are exploring the available tools.
Select a topic to read its instructions and available screenshots or short demonstrations. Back and Forward return to previously viewed topics. Related topics connect nearby tasks.
Reading, searching, and playing a demonstration leave your document unchanged. Close Help to try an action on your own artwork.
Article links use #help/topic. The Help content is bundled with the editor for installed or locally served use. Escape or the close button returns to the canvas.

sections.title: Keyboard shortcuts and accessible use
sections.summary: Use keyboard controls and keep the final artwork readable.
body: V selects whole objects; A selects supported anchors and parts; T adds text; P uses Pen; G edits gradients; Shift+W opens Width Tool. Ctrl+Z undoes; Ctrl+Shift+Z or Ctrl+Y redoes; Ctrl+D duplicates; Ctrl+G groups; Ctrl+Shift+G ungroups. On macOS use Command for the corresponding modifier.

Arrow keys nudge selected artwork or supported selected handles. Shift makes a larger step. Delete removes unlocked selections or selected anchors; when too few anchors remain, it removes the affected path or subpath. Deleting an endpoint of an ordinary line removes that line. Escape cancels an edit or closes the active menu or dialog.

Tab and Shift+Tab move between controls. Enter or Space activates a button. Lines supports arrow-key navigation, Home, End, and Escape. Use labeled slide actions when dragging thumbnails is inconvenient.
Fit artboard restores the page overview. Canvas zoom changes the view rather than exported geometry. Document setup controls grids and snapping; Ctrl or Command bypasses snapping during a gesture.
Labels, contrast, marker shapes, and line styles help readers interpret the scientific content. Do not rely on color alone. Check text and symbols at the final publication or projection size.

sections.title: Troubleshooting
sections.summary: Keep work open and preserve a copy before replacing missing content.
body: If browser save status reports a failure, download the current document before closing the page, then use Retry. If another tab changed the same saved workspace, review the conflict or save a separate copy. Clearing browser data does not recover deleted saves.

If an asset or image is missing, check Source & notes and the available replacement controls. A protected source page or raster image cannot expose individual editable points. Direct Selection works on supported editable vectors, not every visible pixel.

For unexpected PDF or SVG appearance, compare with the original. Try Source-backed placement when you want the page kept intact, or use an original SVG when editable vector geometry is essential. Check fonts, clipping, symbols, and raster portions.
For PowerPoint warnings, keep the original PPTX and inspect the imported or exported deck. Redraw or replace an unsupported object deliberately rather than assuming it was converted faithfully.

If a Windows .fsfigure file opens an older installed editor, use Browser files > Open file in the web app or Open in the intended desktop app. Windows file associations are separate from browser downloads.

If drawing feels constrained, check snapping in Document setup; Ctrl or Command temporarily bypasses it. Use Fit to restore the overview. If import or export fails, keep the document open, save a copy if possible, and include the operation, file type, and visible error when reporting the problem.

sections.title: About Figure Tool
sections.summary: Superbench Figure Tool is a scientific illustration and presentation editor.
body: Figure provides a canvas for scientific diagrams and publication figures. Presentation provides slide decks. Both share drawing, text, assets, selection, appearance, save, and export tools.

The web and desktop editions use the same editor source, but their file access and PDF services differ. Browser saves are local to this device; the web app does not provide an account or cloud synchronization.
This is a beta release. Use About for the current edition’s information and site links. Keep editable document backups and review important imports and exports visually.

First-party software uses Apache-2.0. Original bundled scientific artwork uses CC0-1.0; third-party libraries, fonts, and imported content retain their own terms. See the included license and attribution information.

sections.title: Current limitations
sections.summary: Know where imports, exports, and browser storage need extra care.
body: PDF and SVG import reconstruct supported editable artwork or keep a placed/protected representation. Fonts, spacing, clipping, masks, filters, blends, and complex gradients may differ. A scanned PDF or image cannot recover its original vector paths or plot data.

The static web edition has no native PDF service. Advanced rewriting of attached PDF content is unavailable there. Reconstructed canvas edits are not a guarantee that the original PDF’s internal structure was preserved.

PPTX supports common text, shapes, lines, images, and notes. Complex masters, layouts, charts, SmartArt, tables, media, animation, advanced effects, and arbitrary paths are not fully supported. Mixed character formatting can be reduced. Review all interchange warnings and the receiving application’s result.

Font availability and shaping differ between computers and browsers. Figure Tool does not provide full prepress, color management, font installation, or equivalence with every Illustrator, PowerPoint, or PDF feature.

There is no real-time collaboration, cloud synchronization, direct Google Slides connection, or animation authoring. Browser copies depend on the device, browser profile, origin, available storage, and retained site data.

Export warnings and schematic assets help prepare artwork; they do not assess biological accuracy, infer causal relationships, or validate experimental conclusions. Keep original data and sources, editable document files, and final-size visual review.
